'''Edward Alan Knapp''' (March 7, 1932 – August 17, 2009)<ref name='presidency'>{{cite web|url=https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/ws/index.php?pid=42724 |title=Nomination of Edward A. Knapp To Be an Assistant Director of the National Science Foundation |accessdate=2009-04-14 |date=July 12, 1982 }}</ref> was an American [[physicist]] and was director of the [[National Science Foundation]] from 1982 to 1984.

Knapp graduated with BA from [[Pomona College]] in 1954, and with a PhD in [[physics]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1958.<ref name="thesis-knapp-1959">{{cite thesis |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/301886512/ |title=Angular distribution of photo-pions from hydrogen |date=1959 |publisher=[[University of California, Berkeley]] |type=Ph.D. |last=Knapp |first=Edward Alan |id={{ProQuest|301886512}}|url-access=subscription  |oclc=21754943}}</ref> He then moved to the [[Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory]], where he became division leader of the accelerator technology division.

In 1978, he was a guest scientist in the USA–USSR Exchange Program in Fundamental Properties of Matter.<ref name='presidency'/> He also was a guest scientist in the US–Japanese Cooperative Cancer Research Program (NCI) in 1979.<ref name='presidency'/>

On July 12, 1982, he was nominated by [[Ronald Reagan]] to succeed [[William Klemperer]] as assistant director for the Mathematical and Physical Sciences Directorate of the National Science Foundation. In November 1982, he became director of the [[National Science Foundation|NSF]], succeeding [[John Brooks Slaughter]]. In August 1984, he gave up the position to [[Erich Bloch]] and returned to scientific research.<ref name='nsf'>{{cite web |url=https://www.nsf.gov/about/history/knapp_bio.jsp |title=Edward A. Knapp (NSF biography) |accessdate=2009-04-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606081358/http://www.nsf.gov/about/history/knapp_bio.jsp |archive-date=2011-06-06 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Knapp died at his home in [[Santa Fe, New Mexico]], on August 17, 2009, after battling pancreatic cancer.<ref name="Physics Today">{{cite journal |title=Edward Alan Knapp |journal=[[Physics Today]] |volume=63 |issue=2 |page=57 |year=2010 |doi=10.1063/1.3326995|bibcode=2010PhT....63b..57S |last1 = Simmons|first1 = L. M.}}</ref>
